children: Copart agreed to acquire the automotive marketplace and data services company ACV for $10.50 a share in cash.
The online car auction platform said its price implies an equity value of around $1.9 billion, and represents a roughly 41% premium to ACV's 30-day volume-weighted average price as of Wednesday.

The deal is expected to be neutral to Copart's earnings per share in the first full year of ownership and accretive thereafter, and should also generate near-term cost and revenue synergies, Copart said.
The deal, which will be executed through a tender offer and has been approved by the boards of both companies, is expected to close by the end of the year.
ACV will remain an independent subsidiary within Copart and retain its existing leadership team.

"This acquisition reflects a significant milestone in our growth strategy by creating an industry-leading end-to-end vehicle remarketing platform that is fully digital," Chief Executive Officer Jay Adair said.
ACV shares surged 43% to $10.33 in after-hours trading on Thursday. Shares in Copart were up 9.5% at $33.66.
The deal came as Copart reported a lower profit and growing revenue in the fourth quarter.
The company reported a profit of $327.4 million, or 35 cents a share, compared with $396.4 million, or 41 cents a share, a year earlier.
Copart's total revenue rose 2.4% to $1.15 billion. Service revenue grew 1.4% to $969.5 million, while vehicle sales jumped 8.3% to $182.9 million.
Analysts polled by FactSet were expecting a profit of 38 cents a share on $1.14 billion in total revenue.
